verdict.line: You lose trades before level 6 whenever Renekton's Fury hits 50 for the empowered stun combo; you win once you've itemized burst and start answering his all-ins instead of starting them.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Fury bar is the whole matchup: at 50 Fury his W (Ruthless Predator) becomes a 3-hit, shield-destroying 1.5s stun and his Q (Cull the Meek) heals harder, letting him win extended exchanges Riven can't out-damage before level 6. That's why OP.GG logs this as defensive with Renekton favored for both the lane and the solo kill at a 46.7% Riven win rate over 1442 games — the fix is to deny him free Fury, not to out-trade him cold.

theirWindow.what: His W now lands a 1.5s stun through shields and his Q heal spikes. Disengage with E (Valor) or step past 300 range rather than standing in it.

yourWindow.when: After his E (Slice and Dice) is down
yourWindow.what: Slice and Dice is a 16-10s cooldown dash with no other gap closer behind it — once he's spent it to engage or reset wave, step in with Q (Broken Wings) into W (Ki Burst) for a stun he can't escape.

powerCurve.note: his Q poke and W stun land first
your R and Conqueror offset his sustain
Death's Dance and Wind Slash out-scale him

start.why: The 46% win rate, 88.4% pick path — the extra HP and sustain are what let you survive his Q/W pokes while you wait out the Fury-dump levels.

boots.why: 51.5% pick, 44.2% win rate — flat physical reduction blunts his empowered W auto and the follow-up Q/E of his all-in combo.

core.why: Highest-performing core start (68.1% win rate) — the shield and execute damage answer his burst rather than racing it.
Converts the burst from his empowered W+Q combo into damage over time, which is the single biggest thing that flips this matchup past level 6.
Sustain and waveclear to keep you even on resources through the levels he's fed on Fury off trades.

situational.when: they start stacking armor to wall off your damage
you're ahead and want faster R resets for repeated skirmishes
you want onhit sustain in prolonged trades instead of pure burst

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking adaptive healing in extended trades is your direct counter to his Q self-heal and Fury-fed all-ins — it's what lets you stay in skirmishes instead of being out-sustained.

summoners.why: 92.7% pick rate at 46.5% win rate — Ignite's grievous wounds directly undercuts his Q heal and punishes any all-in he commits Fury to.

playing.title: Track the Fury bar, not just HP
playing.detail: At 50 Fury his W (Ruthless Predator) becomes a 1.5s stun that strips shields. Don't contest a trade if he's near that threshold.

playing.title: Use E (Valor) to absorb, not to chase
playing.detail: Valor's forward dash (cooldown 10/9/8/7/6s) blocks incoming damage — spend it on his engage hit, not to close distance on him.

playing.title: Punish the gap after his E
playing.detail: Slice and Dice sits on a 16-10s cooldown with no backup dash. Once he's used it, step in with Q (Broken Wings) into W (Ki Burst).

playing.title: Never extend into his Q heal
playing.detail: Cull the Meek heals him on a 7s cooldown every cast. Burst and disengage instead of trading auto-for-auto.

playing.title: Hold R for his all-in, not yours
playing.detail: Blade of the Exile costs 120/90s on its first two casts — save Wind Slash to finish a fight he starts rather than opening with it.

playing.title: Freeze and deny Fury pre-6
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read is defensive for a reason: fall back level 1-5, don't let him farm Fury off free autos, then flip the lane once your core items land.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the Fury-threshold reasoning and trade timing are my own tactical read on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Engage Renekton while keeping an eye out for his Fury. Use your abilities to deal burst damage and fall back to slowly gain control over lane.
